tools.name: wpconvert_convert_folder
tools.description: Zip a local folder (excluding node_modules, build output, and secrets by default) and start a WordPress theme conversion. Call wpconvert_quota first to review capabilities (mode, credits, download availability). Returns a jobId and an idempotency_key. Leave idempotency_key blank for a new intentional conversion. If a prior call may have timed out or returned an ambiguous network error, retry with the exact idempotency_key returned by that prior call — do not omit it and do not invent a new one. Do not reuse a key for changed files, options, or a deliberate new conversion. Once you have a jobId, poll wpconvert_check_status until "done", then follow recommended_next for download or preview. Without an API key it uses the guest session from wpconvert_connect (free previews, up to 50MB zipped); with neither it returns recommended_next wpconvert_connect.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the folder to convert.

type.description: Export type. Only "theme" is supported right now.

maxAssetSizeMB.description: Exclude individual files larger than this many MB.

idempotency_key.description: Leave blank for a new intentional conversion. If a prior call may have timed out or returned an ambiguous network error, retry with the exact idempotency_key returned by that prior call. Do not reuse a key for changed files, options, or a deliberate new conversion.

tools.name: wpconvert_check_status
tools.description: Check the status of a conversion job. Returns persisted status per the OpenAPI ConversionStatus enum (queued, analyzing, building, rendering, labeling, generating, validating, uploading, done, failed). The tool-layer bucket `processing` means still in progress — it is not a persisted API value. Also returns progress, download/preview availability, and recommended_next (which tool to call next). When done and downloadable, recommended_next points to wpconvert_download_result; for preview-only jobs it points to wpconvert_create_preview instead.

tools.name: wpconvert_download_result
tools.description: Download a completed conversion to disk. Only use when wpconvert_check_status shows download_available and recommended_next is wpconvert_download_result. Returns the saved file path. For preview-only jobs, use wpconvert_create_preview or upgrade and re-convert instead.

outDir.description: Directory to save into (default: current directory).

tools.name: wpconvert_create_preview
tools.description: Create a WordPress Playground preview link for a completed conversion so the user can view the theme running in a live, in-browser WordPress (no local install). Returns a URL the user must open in a browser — you cannot embed or render it yourself. The link expires after about ten minutes and grants temporary access to the theme, so treat it as sensitive.

tools.name: wpconvert_explain_failure
tools.description: Return the failure reason for a failed conversion job. Distinguishes status retries, recovering a submission with the same idempotency_key via wpconvert_convert_folder, and starting a deliberate new conversion without that key.

tools.name: wpconvert_quota
tools.description: Show account quota, capabilities (conversion mode, can_start, download availability), and recommended_next. Call this before wpconvert_convert_folder to understand what the next conversion will consume. For a guest session it shows the free previews left.

tools.name: wpconvert_connect
tools.description: Connect WPConvert without an API key. kind "guest": the user confirms they are human once in the browser and gets a few free previews (no account; downloads need a purchase). kind "login": the user signs in or creates an account in the browser and types the code shown, and a new API key is saved locally. Returns a link and a short code. Show both to the user and ask them to open the link; never open it yourself. Then call wpconvert_connect_status.

kind.description: "guest" for free previews, "login" to use a WPConvert account (needed to buy).

tools.name: wpconvert_connect_status
tools.description: Check whether the user finished the wpconvert_connect link (waits up to about 20 seconds). Call it again while it says "waiting". Also reports how WPConvert is connected now: guest (with previews left) or account (with a masked email). Never returns the token or key.

tools.name: wpconvert_plans
tools.description: List what the user can buy: Starter (unlock one theme), Pro, Agency (monthly or yearly) and pay-as-you-go credit packs, with what each includes and today's price. Pass jobId to see options for unlocking that conversion. Show all options to the user and let them choose; do not pick for them. Then call wpconvert_checkout with the checkout_arguments of their choice.

tools.name: wpconvert_checkout
tools.description: Create a Stripe checkout link for the option the user picked from wpconvert_plans. Call this only after the user has chosen; pass that choice's checkout_arguments unchanged. Needs a signed-in account (wpconvert_connect kind "login"). Returns a link the user opens to pay; never open it yourself and never pay on their behalf.

jobId.description: Conversion to unlock. Required for starter.
